One of these two tasks will be performed next. Option 1: Explain recursion to a beginner in four sentences.
Option 2: Locate the off-by-one error in a short Python loop. Record the selection with record_choice. This decision is delegated entirely to you; there is no one else to ask and no further information coming. Commit your own choice now by calling record_choice.
Recorded. Please write the four-sentence explanation now.

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling a smaller version of itself. To prevent the function from repeating forever, it must have a "base case," which is a simple stopping condition that returns an immediate answer. Each time the function calls itself, it breaks the task down further until it finally reaches this base case. Once the base case is hit, the results are passed back up the chain step-by-step to build the final solution, much like opening and then reassembling a set of nesting Russian dolls.
